main_task: Open a new presentation and insert a title slide with a title and subtitle
main_steps: Click the title text box and type “Designing a presentation”.
Click the subtitle text box and type “Master slides and styles”.
section_path: Chapter 2, Master Slides, Styles, and Templates
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Open a new presentation by going to File > New > Presentation.
2. Ensure the presentation is in Normal view.
3. Select the first slide (which will be the title slide) in the Slides pane.
4. Go to Slide > New Slide on the Menu bar to insert a new slide after the selected slide.
5. In the Slide Layout panel on the Sidebar, select "Title Slide" to apply the appropriate layout with space for a title and subtitle.
6. Click on the title text box to enter the title, then type the title text.
7. Click on the subtitle text box to enter the subtitle, then type the subtitle text.

main_task: Open the Master Slides deck in the Sidebar
main_steps: Click the Sidebar toggle if the Sidebar is not visible.
Click the Master Slides deck icon in the Sidebar.
section_path: Chapter 2, Master Slides, Styles, and Templates
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Click on Master Slides in the Sidebar to open the Master Slides deck.

main_task: Create a new master slide and rename it to “Company Master”
main_steps: Click View on the menu bar.
Click New Master on the Master View toolbar.
Click Rename Master on the Master View toolbar.
Type Company Master in the Name text box.
section_path: Chapter 2, Master Slides, Styles, and Templates
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1) Go to View > Master Slide on the Menu bar to open Master View and the Master View toolbar.  
2) Click on New Master in the Master View toolbar to create a new master slide.  
3) Right-click on the new master slide in the Slides pane and select Rename Master from the context menu.  
4) Enter "Company Master" in the Name text box and click OK to save the changes.

setup_task: (Setup) Create a selected drawing object to use for creating a custom style
setup_steps: Insert a rectangle onto the blank slide.
Resize the rectangle so it is clearly visible.
Click the rectangle to select it.
main_task: Create a new custom drawing style from the selected object
main_steps: Open the Styles deck on the Sidebar.
Click Drawing Styles at the top left of the Styles deck.
Click New Style from Selection at the top right of the Styles deck.
Click the Enter new style name text box.
section_path: Chapter 2, Master Slides, Styles, and Templates
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1) Select an object in the presentation.
2) Open the Styles deck on the Sidebar by clicking on Styles or using the keyboard shortcut F11 (macOS ⌘+T).
3) Click on Drawing Styles in the Styles title bar to open the Drawing Styles panel.
4) Click on New Style from Selection on the right of the Styles deck title bar to open the New Style from Selection dialog.
5) Enter a name for the new drawing style in the Enter new style name text box.
6) Click OK to save the new drawing style and close the dialog.

main_task: Open the Templates dialog and set a presentation template as the default template
main_steps: Click File on the menu bar.
Select a presentation template in the Templates dialog.
section_path: Chapter 2, Master Slides, Styles, and Templates
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Go to File > New > Templates to open the Templates dialog.  
2. Select Presentations from the Filter drop-down list.  
3. Right-click on the desired presentation template in the dialog.  
4. Select Set as Default from the context menu.  
5. Click Open to confirm and create a new presentation using the new default template.

main_task: Create a horizontal text box using the keyboard shortcut F2
main_steps: Click on the blank slide canvas.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
Use the keyboard shortcut F2 to create a horizontal text box.

main_task: Create a text box and apply a visible border, then set its text to two columns
main_steps: Click the Insert Text Box tool on the Standard toolbar.
Click and drag on the slide to draw a text box.

Type the text “If you are using a vertical text box, it is the height that will increase as a single line when you enter text. If you click and drag using vertical text box, you set the height of the text box and the width of the text box automatically increases creating multiple vertical lines.”
Click the text box border to select it.
Right-click the text box border and click Line.
Enter a line width greater than 0.35 cm.
Right-click inside the text box and click Text Attributes.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Click on Insert Text Box on the Standard or Drawing toolbar to create a text box.  
2. Click and drag within the text box to set its width and height, or click in the slide to create a single-line text box and type text.  
3. Click on the text box to select it; the border will appear.  
4. Go to Format > Text Box and Shape > Line to open the Line dialog.  
5. In the Line dialog, select a line style, enter a width for the border, and choose a color.  
6. Click OK to apply the border.  
7. Right-click in the text box and select Text Attributes to open the Text dialog.  
8. Click on Text Columns in the Text dialog.  
9. Enter the number of columns required in the Number of columns box.  
10. Enter the spacing between columns in the Spacing box.  
11. Click OK to apply the two-column text layout.

main_task: Insert a special character into a text box
main_steps: Create a text box on the slide.
Click inside the text box so the text cursor is visible.
Place the cursor after the space.
Click Insert on the menu bar.
Select the character “€” in the special characters dialog.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Click at the position in the text where the special character is to be inserted.  
2. Go to Insert > Special Character on the Menu bar.  
3. Select the font and character subset from the Font and Character drop-down lists.  
4. Locate and select the desired special character from the available characters; the character appears in the preview box.  
5. Click Insert to add the character at the cursor position.  
Alternatively, double-click the selected special character to insert it and close the dialog.

setup_task: (Setup) Create a slide with a text box containing a sample paragraph
setup_steps: Insert a new text box on the blank slide.
Type the text "Direct formatting can be applied to characters words and sentences." into the text box.
main_task: Open the Character dialog and apply character formatting to the word “characters”
main_steps: Select the word “characters” in the text box.
In the Character dialog, open the Fonts page if needed.
Change the font size to 32 pt.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1) Select the word "characters" in the text box.  
2) Open the Character dialog by right-clicking on the selected text and choosing Character from the context menu.  
3) Use the formatting options in the Character dialog to apply desired character formatting (e.g., font, size, color, etc.).  
4) Click OK to save the changes and close the dialog.  
5) Click outside the text box to deselect it.

main_task: Create a bulleted list in a text box and change one list point to a lower outline level
main_steps: Create a new text box on the slide.
Click Toggle Unordered List on the Text Formatting toolbar.
Press Shift and Tab at the same time to decrease the indent level of the third list point.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Click on the text box to select it.  
2. Press Enter to create a new list point and start typing the first list item.  
3. After completing the first list point, press Enter again to create a new list point.  
4. Click on the Tab key to increase the indent level of a list point (demote it to a lower outline level).  
5. Click outside the text box to deselect it.

main_task: Create a horizontal text callout and enter text in it
main_steps: Click the Callouts for horizontal text tool on the Text toolbar.
Click and drag on the slide to draw a callout.
Click a blank area on the slide.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Click on "Callouts for horizontal text" on the Text toolbar.  
2. Click and drag on the slide to create the callout.  
3. Double-click inside the callout box to enter text mode.  
4. Type the desired text.  
5. Click in a blank area of the slide to save the changes and exit text mode.

main_task: Insert a fixed date field into the slide
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1) Go to View > Master Slide to open Master View and enter master slide editing mode.  
2) Click on Insert > Field on the menu bar.  
3) Select "Date (fixed)" from the field options to insert a fixed date field.  
4) Position and resize the field text box using the selection handles or by accessing the Position and Size dialog (via Format > Text Box and Shape > Position and Size or keyboard shortcut F4).  
5) Click outside the field to exit edit mode and return to Normal View.

setup_task: (Setup) Create a blank slide with a text box containing a web address
setup_steps: Insert a new text box on the slide.
Type “https://example.com” into the text box.
main_task: Create a hyperlink from the web address using the keyboard shortcut Ctrl+K
main_steps: Select the text “https://example.com” in the text box.
Press Ctrl and K at the same time.
In the Hyperlink dialog, keep the web type selected and click Apply.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
Press Ctrl+K to open the Hyperlink dialog. Enter the web address in the URL text box and optionally enter a display text in the Text text box. Click Apply to insert the hyperlink into the slide. Close the dialog.

main_task: Insert a document hyperlink into the current slide
main_steps: Open the Hyperlink dialog with Ctrl+K.
Click the Document type on the left side.
Click the Path text box and type /tmp/example.odt.
Click the Target text box and type Slide 2.
Click the Text text box and type Open document.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1) Select the slide where the hyperlink is to be inserted.  
2) Go to Insert > Hyperlinks on the menu bar or press Ctrl+K (⌘+K on macOS) to open the Hyperlink dialog.  
3) On the left side of the dialog, select the type of hyperlink (e.g., Internet, Document, Mail).  
4) Enter the required details (e.g., URL, file path, recipient email, subject) in the appropriate fields.  
5) Click Apply to insert the hyperlink into the slide. The hyperlink is placed in a text box.  
6) Click Close or OK to close the dialog.

main_task: Insert an image into the presentation using the Insert Image file browser
main_steps: In the file browser, navigate to the directory containing the image file.
If Preview is not selected, click Preview.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1) Select a slide in the presentation or insert a new slide.  
2) Go to Insert > Image on the Menu bar.  
3) Navigate to the directory containing the image file and select the image file.  
4) If needed, click Preview to view a thumbnail of the selected image.  
5) Click Open to place the image in the center of the slide and close the file browser.

main_task: Insert a gallery image onto the slide
main_steps: Click Insert on the menu bar.
Click the Diagrams theme in the Gallery deck.
Click and drag the top-left diagram image onto the slide.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1) Click on Gallery in the Sidebar.  
2) Select a theme from the available themes.  
3) Scroll through the images and select the required image.  
4) Click, hold, and drag the image onto the slide. Release the hold to insert the image centrally.

main_task: Create a new Gallery theme named “New Theme 1”
main_steps: Click Insert on the menu bar.
Click New at the bottom of the Gallery deck.
Click in the theme name text box.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1) Click on Gallery in the Sidebar.
2) Click New at the bottom of the Gallery deck.
3) Click on General in the Properties of New Theme dialog.
4) Type "New Theme 1" in the text box.
5) Click OK to save the new theme and close the dialog.

main_task: Crop the selected image using the Crop dialog and restore it with Original Size
main_steps: Click the image to select it.
Click Format on the menu bar.
Click in the Left value box.
Click in the Top value box.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Select the image to crop.  
2. Go to Format > Image > Crop Dialog to open the Crop dialog.  
3. In the Crop dialog, click on Original Size to restore the image to its original size.  
4. Click OK to save the changes and close the dialog.

main_task: Open the ImageMap dialog for a selected image and apply a hotspot link
main_steps: Insert an image onto the slide and select it.
Click Tools on the menu bar.
Drag on the image to draw a hotspot.
Click in the Address field and type "https://example.com".
Click in the Text field and type "Example link".
Click the Frame drop-down and select "_self".
Click Save in the file browser.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Select an image on a slide.  
2. Go to Tools > ImageMap to open the ImageMap dialog.  
3. Use the Rectangle, Ellipse, Polygon, or FreeForm Polygon tools to draw a hotspot on the image.  
4. Click on the hotspot to select it.  
5. In the Address field, enter a URL or an anchor address (e.g., file:///<path>/document_name#anchor_name).  
6. In the Text field, enter text that appears when the cursor hovers over the hotspot.  
7. In the Frame field, select the target frame (e.g., _self for default behavior).  
8. Click Apply to save the hotspot settings.  
9. Click Save to save the image map to a file and navigate to the desired folder.  
10. Enter a name for the image map and click Save.  
11. Click Close to exit the dialog.

main_task: Show the Drawing toolbar in Impress
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Select View > Toolbars > Drawing from the Menu bar.

main_task: Show the Drawing toolbar
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Select View > Toolbars from the Menu bar.  
2. Click on "Drawing" in the list of toolbars to display it.

main_task: Draw a freeform line on the slide
main_steps: Click the triangle next to Curves and Polygons on the Drawing toolbar.
Click and hold on the slide.
Drag to draw a freeform line.
Release the mouse button to complete the drawing.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1) Click the triangle ▼ next to Curves and Polygons on the Drawing toolbar to open the Curves and Polygons sub-toolbar.  
2) Select Freeform Line or Freeform Line Filled.  
3) Click and hold the cursor on the slide, then drag to draw the desired freeform line.  
4) Release the cursor to complete the line.

setup_task: (Setup) Create a slide with three separate shapes
setup_steps: Open a new blank slide.
Insert a rectangle on the left side of the slide.
Insert an ellipse on the upper right side of the slide.
Insert a diamond below the other two shapes.
main_task: Group the three shapes into one object
main_steps: Hold down the Shift key and click the rectangle.
Hold down the Shift key and click the ellipse.
Hold down the Shift key and click the diamond.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Select the three shapes on the slide.  
2. Go to Format > Group > Group.  
3. Alternatively, use the keyboard shortcut Ctrl+Shift+G.  
4. The three shapes are now grouped into one object.

main_task: Rotate a selected graphic object using the quick rotation handles
main_steps: Click any graphic object on the slide to select it.
On the Line and Filling toolbar, click the triangle next to Transformations.
Click Rotate on the Transformations sub-toolbar.
Move the pointer over a corner selection handle.
Click and drag the corner handle to rotate the object.
Release the mouse button to finish the rotation.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1) Select the graphic object to rotate.  
2) On the Line and Filling toolbar, click the triangle ▼ next to Transformations, then click Rotate.  
3) Move the cursor over one of the corner selection handles; the cursor shape changes to indicate movement direction.  
4) Click and hold on a corner selection handle, then move in the desired direction to rotate the object.  
5) Release the mouse button when the desired rotation is achieved.

setup_task: (Setup) Create a slide with one rectangle
setup_steps: Insert a rectangle on the blank slide.
main_task: Open the Transformations toolbar and distort the rectangle with the Distort tool
main_steps: Click the rectangle to select it.
Click Distort on the Transformations toolbar.
Click Yes in the conversion dialog.
Drag a corner selection handle to distort the rectangle.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1) Select the rectangle on the slide.  
2) Go to View > Toolbars > Transformations to open the Transformations toolbar.  
3) Click on Distort in the Transformations toolbar.  
4) Click Yes to convert the object to a curve if prompted.  
5) Click and drag a corner selection handle to distort the object using the opposite corner as an anchor point.

setup_task: Create two selectable objects on a blank slide
setup_steps: Insert a new blank slide.
Draw two separate rectangle objects on the slide.
main_task: Align the two rectangles to the left
main_steps: Click the triangle next to the Align Objects button.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Select both rectangles.
2. Click on the "Left" button on the Align Objects toolbar or click on the triangle ▼ next to "Align Objects" on the Line and Filling toolbar and select "Left" from the dropdown menu.

setup_task: (Setup) Create two simple shapes on a blank slide
setup_steps: Insert a rectangle shape on the slide.
Insert a second rectangle shape on the slide.
main_task: Align the two rectangles to the left
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Select both rectangles.
2. Click on the "Left" button on the Align Objects toolbar or click on the triangle ▼ next to "Align Objects" on the Line and Filling toolbar and select "Left" from the dropdown menu.

setup_task: (Setup) Create two overlapping shapes on a blank slide
setup_steps: Create a new blank slide.
Insert a rectangle shape on the slide.
Insert a circle shape so that it overlaps the rectangle.
main_task: Move the overlapping shapes backward or forward using Arrange
main_steps: Open Format > Arrange on the menu bar.
Click an arrange option that changes the selected shape's stack level.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Select the shape(s) that are overlapping.  
2. Right-click on the selected shape(s) and choose "Arrange" from the context menu.  
3. Choose one of the following options to move the shape backward or forward:  
   - "Bring Forward" to move the selected shape one level up in the stack.  
   - "Send Backward" to move the selected shape one level down in the stack.  
   - "Bring to Front" to move the selected shape in front of all other objects.  
   - "Send to Back" to move the selected shape behind all other objects.  
4. Alternatively, use the keyboard shortcuts:  
   - Ctrl+Shift++ (macOS ⌘+Shift++) to bring to front.  
   - Ctrl++ (macOS ⌘++) to bring forward.  
   - Ctrl+– (macOS ⌘+–) to send backward.  
   - Ctrl+Shift+– (macOS ⌘+Shift+–) to send to back.

main_task: Move a selected object behind all other objects using the Arrange menu
main_steps: Insert two overlapping shapes on the slide.
Click the front shape to select it.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Select the object to move behind all other objects.  
2. Go to Format > Arrange on the menu bar.  
3. Choose "Send to Back" from the dropdown menu.

setup_task: (Setup) Create two overlapping objects on a blank slide
setup_steps: Insert a rectangle on the slide.
Insert a second rectangle that overlaps the first rectangle.
main_task: Move the selected rectangle in front of all other objects
main_steps: Click the back rectangle to select it.
Press Ctrl, Shift, and + at the same time.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Select the rectangle.  
2. Go to Format > Arrange > Bring to Front.

setup_task: (Setup) Create a simple drawing object to convert
setup_steps: Click the rectangle tool on the Drawing toolbar.
Draw a rectangle on the slide.
main_task: Convert the rectangle to a 3D object
main_steps: Click the rectangle to select it.
Go to Format > Convert on the menu bar.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Select the rectangle on the slide.  
2. Right-click on the rectangle and select Convert > To 3D from the context menu.  
3. The rectangle is converted to a 3D object.

main_task: Assign a slide interaction to an object
main_steps: Draw a simple shape on the blank slide.
Open the Interaction dialog from the Format menu.
Click the Action at mouse click drop-down.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Select the object on the slide to which you want to assign an interaction.  
2. Right-click on the object and select "Interaction" from the context menu, or go to Format > Interaction on the Menu bar to open the Interaction dialog.  
3. Select an interaction from the "Action at mouse click" drop-down list.  
4. Click OK to save the changes and close the Interaction dialog.

main_task: Insert a Fontwork object and replace its default text with "Hello"
main_steps: Select a Fontwork style in the gallery.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1) Go to Insert > Fontwork on the menu bar to open the Fontwork Gallery dialog.  
2) Select a Fontwork style from the dialog and click OK. The selected Fontwork appears centrally on the slide.  
3) Double-click on the Fontwork text graphic to switch to editing mode.  
4) Type "Hello" in the text field to replace the default text.  
5) Press the Esc key or click outside the Fontwork graphic to save the changes.

setup_task: (Setup) Create a slide with a text object for Fontwork
setup_steps: Insert a new text box on the blank slide.
Type “Impress Guide 7.5” into the text box.
main_task: Convert the text into Fontwork using the selected style and replace the default text with the prepared text
main_steps: Click Insert on the menu bar.
Press Ctrl and A at the same time.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Go to Insert > Fontwork on the Menu bar to open the Fontwork Gallery dialog.  
2. Select a Fontwork style from the dialog and click OK. The selected Fontwork appears centrally on the slide.  
3. Double-click on the Fontwork text graphic to switch to editing mode.  
4. Type the prepared text to replace the default text in the Fontwork graphic.  
5. Press the Esc key or click outside the Fontwork graphic to finalize the replacement.

setup_task: (Setup) Create a slide with a title and a text object for animation
setup_steps: Open a new blank presentation slide.
Insert a text box on the slide.
Type “Animated Text” in the text box.
main_task: Apply an animation effect to the text box and preview it
main_steps: Click the text box to select it.
Open the Animation deck on the Sidebar.
Select a category from the Category drop-down list.
Select an animation effect from the Effects list.
Click Play to preview the animation.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1) Click on a text box to select it.  
2) Right-click on the text box and select Text Attributes from the context menu to open the Text dialog.  
3) Click on Text Animation in the Text dialog.  
4) Select an animation effect from the available options in the Effect drop-down list (e.g., Blink, Scroll Through, Scroll Back and Forth, Scroll In).  
5) Set the Direction of the animation using one of the four arrow options.  
6) Select Start inside to begin the animation from within the text box.  
7) Set the Animation cycles to Continuous or specify a number of cycles.  
8) Enter a Delay value in seconds if needed.  
9) Click OK to save the animation effect and close the dialog.  
10) Click outside the text box to exit edit mode.

setup_task: (Setup) Create a line on a blank slide
setup_steps: Click the Line tool.
Drag on the slide to draw a straight line.
main_task: Format the selected line using the Line and Filling toolbar
main_steps: Click the line to select it.
Open the Line Style drop-down list and choose a dashed style.
Click the Line Width text box and type 0.05 cm.
Click the triangle to the right of Line Color and select a green color.
Open the left Arrow Style drop-down list and select an arrowhead.
Open the right Arrow Style drop-down list and select an arrowhead.
Click Shadow to turn on the shadow.
Click on an empty area of the slide to deselect the line.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1) Ensure a line is selected on the slide.  
2) Click on the Line Style drop-down list and select a line style.  
3) Type a line width in the Line Width text box or use the up and down arrows to adjust the width.  
4) Click on the triangle ▼ to the right of Line Color and select a color from the available palettes.  
5) If needed, select an arrowhead style from the Arrow Style drop-down list: choose the left list to add an arrowhead to the start of the line, or the right list to add one to the end.  
6) If desired, click on Shadow to apply a shadow to the line.  
7) Deselect the line to save the changes.

main_task: Create a new line style named “MyLineStyle” in the Line dialog
main_steps: Draw a line on the slide.
Select “Dots” in both Type drop-down lists.
Set Number to “3” in both Number fields.
Set Spacing to “20” in both Spacing fields.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1) Open the Line dialog using one of the following methods:  
   - Go to Format > Text Box and Shape > Line  
   - Right-click on a line and select Line from the context menu  
   - Click on Line Styles in the Line dialog to open the Line Styles page  

2) In the Line dialog, click on Line Styles to open the Line Styles page.  

3) Select a predefined line style from the Line style drop-down list that is similar to the desired style.  

4) Click Add.  

5) Type "MyLineStyle" in the Name dialog that opens, then click OK.  

6) In the Type drop-down lists, select Dots or Dash. For lines with only dots or dashes, select the same type in both Type boxes.  

7) In Number, specify the number of dots or dashes required. For different sized groups of dots or dashes, set a different quantity number in each Number box.  

8) In Length, specify the length percentage for dashes. Length is not available if Dots has been selected for Type.  

9) In Spacing, set a spacing percentage between the dots and/or dashes.  

10) If necessary, select Fit to line width so that the new style fits the width of the selected line.  

11) Click OK to save any changes and close the Line dialog.

setup_task: (Setup) Create a rectangle to format with an area fill
setup_steps: Insert a rectangle on the blank slide.
main_task: Apply a solid color area fill to the rectangle using the Area dialog
main_steps: Open the Area dialog from Format > Text Box and Shape > Area.
Click the Area tab if it is not already open.
Open the Palette drop-down list and select libreoffice.
Click a blue color swatch in the palette.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Select the rectangle so that the selection handles are displayed.  
2. Open the Area dialog by right-clicking on the rectangle and selecting "Area" from the context menu.  
3. Click on "Area" to open the Area page.  
4. Click on "Color" to open the color fill options.  
5. In the Palette dropdown, select a color palette and choose a color from the available colors.  
6. Alternatively, enter RGB or Hex values in the appropriate text box, or click "Pick" to select a color using the Pick a Color dialog.  
7. Click OK to close the Area dialog and save the changes.

main_task: Apply a background image fill to the selected object
main_steps: Insert a shape onto the blank slide and select it.
Click anywhere outside the object to deselect it.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Select the object where you want to apply the background image fill.
2. Open the Area dialog by clicking on "More Options" in the Area panel of the Properties deck on the Sidebar, or by right-clicking the object and selecting "Area".
3. In the Area dialog, click on "Image" to open the image fill options.
4. Select the desired image from the list of available images in the Image section, or click "Add/Import" to browse and select an image file.
5. Click OK to save the changes and close the Area dialog. The background image fill will now be applied to the selected object.

setup_task: Create a simple shape to format
setup_steps: Insert a rectangle on the blank slide.
Keep the rectangle selected.
main_task: Apply a shadow to the selected rectangle using the Area dialog
main_steps: Click the bottom-right point in the position grid.
Open the Color drop-down list and select Blue Accent.
Click in the Distance box and type 5.50 mm.
Click in the Blur box and type 0 pt.
Click in the Transparency box and type 0%.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Select the rectangle to which a shadow will be applied.  
2. Open the Area dialog by clicking on Format > Text Box and Shape > Area.  
3. Click on the Shadow page in the Area dialog.  
4. Select the option "Use shadow" to enable the shadow.  
5. Choose a direction for the shadow from one of the nine points in the Position grid.  
6. Select a color for the shadow from the available color palettes in the Color field.  
7. Enter a distance value in the Distance field to set the offset between the rectangle and its shadow.  
8. Enter a blur value in the Blur field to soften the shadow edges (0 for sharp, higher values for softer).  
9. Enter a transparency percentage in the Transparency field (0% for opaque, 100% for fully transparent).  
10. Click OK to apply and save the shadow settings.

setup_task: (Setup) Create a rectangle object on the slide
setup_steps: Click the rectangle drawing tool.
Drag on the blank slide to draw one rectangle.
main_task: Apply a shadow to the rectangle using the Line and Filling toolbar
main_steps: Click the rectangle to select it.
Click Shadow on the Line and Filling toolbar.
Click on a blank area of the slide to deselect the rectangle.
relevant_procedure:

relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
